body: In the 1960s, reaching Neptune strained **propellant** budgets; a direct flight could take thirty years. Yet Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune were approaching a **configuration**, an **alignment** recurring every 175 years. Its launch windows let designers **stitch** encounters into a **unified** **itinerary**. Grand Tour **reconnaissance** through those flybys **promised** reduced flight time, **launcher** requirements and **expenditure**. Computation made the geometry **usable**. At JPL, Michael Minovitch developed **ballistic** **multi-planet** trajectories; in 1965 Gary Flandro analysed the outer-planet **opportunity**. The manoeuvre has a long **pedigree** and **unsettled** origins; claims of sole **authorship** mislead. Those contributions transformed **fleeting** **celestial** geometry into mission architecture; each encounter made the next world **attainable**. Near a planet, a craft follows a **curve**. Speed gained **inbound** is lost **outbound**, a **reciprocal** pattern in the planet's **co-moving** frame. Yet gravity **bends** its velocity **vector**. In the Sun's frame, **adding** planetary orbital velocity turns that deflection into a change in **kinetic** energy. Angular momentum changes hands; the planet's response is **imperceptible**. Voyager 2 launched in 1977. Jupiter in 1979 **pushed** it towards Saturn; Saturn in 1981 bent it towards Uranus; Uranus in 1986 sent it towards Neptune in 1989. Each **approach** required precise **targeting** at a prescribed **epoch**. A course **adjustment** could shift **downstream** geometry years later. **Designers** weighed ten thousand **candidate** **trajectories**; the four waypoints were one **cascade**. Gravity assist is no **perpetual-motion** trick. Passing behind a moving planet can **augment** Sun-relative speed; passing ahead can **decelerate** it. **Conservation** holds: the planet **loses** or receives a **minuscule** share of orbital energy. Rockets handled launch and **trim** burns; the propellant **limitation** remained, but the route became an **asset**, supplementing rocket **propulsion**.
